response: Coeliac disease screening in risk groups is justified. According to available data, long-term dietary compliance in screen-detected patients was good, and their quality of life and bone mineral density were comparable to those in non-coeliac subjects and the general population. Active screening in coeliac disease risk groups seems to be reasonable rather than harmful. This suggests that screening can help identify individuals with coeliac disease, allowing them to receive timely treatment and management, which can improve their overall health outcomes.
